description:
A Master Knot Maker Reviving Korea’s Traditional Beauty with a Single Thread

Hello, this is King Process.
From fine threads to intricate knots and flowing tassels, this video introduces the beauty of traditional Korean knotting through the work of Park Yang-ja, an officially recognized master of the craft in Gyeonggi Province, Korea.

Park began learning traditional knotting from master Kim Hee-jin while working in the curatorial department of the National Museum of Korea. She has continued creating and teaching ever since. In 2024, she was officially recognized as a holder of Gyeonggi Province’s Intangible Cultural Heritage in traditional knot making. Through her work and teaching, she passes these skills on to others.

Korea’s history of decorative cords and tassels can be traced in ancient Goguryeo tomb murals. Anak Tomb No. 3, built in AD 357, depicts curtains tied with cords and tassel decorations. These images show how such ornaments were used to decorate living spaces nearly 1
